data.note:
Emetine unblinded: conclusion Protein synthesis correct (NSC 4/4, similarity 0.70-0.81 vs 0.83 top reference). Phenotype: extreme nuclear shape loss (nuc_solidity z -33 to -55, form_factor -31 to -44, eccentricity +11-14), frac_multinucleate_proxy +12.6 to +18.9, cell_count -9.7 to -11.9, actin/tubulin texture high. Microscopist favored Aurora kinase inhibitors due to enlarged lobed/multilobed nuclei mimicking failed cytokinesis/polyploidy, but NSC consistently matched protein synthesis reference compounds (cycloheximide/anisomycin) at all doses 0.3-30 µM, with stable dose-independent defects.

Reflection: Protein synthesis inhibition fits emetine (PubChem CID 10219, BBBC021 Protein synthesis). Emetine is classical eukaryotic translation elongation inhibitor blocking ribosome translocation. Literature supports: Pestka review of ribosome function inhibitors PMID:4949424, structural basis for emetine inhibition of ribosome translocation in Toxoplasma PMID:42539200, translation elongation inhibitors class stabilization of short-lived transcripts PMID:39293933, and eukaryotic elongation system sensitivity PMID:8618948. Morphological overlap with Aurora phenotype likely reflects stress-induced nuclear irregularity and cell shrinkage/decreased density rather than true Aurora mitotic failure, underscoring value of unbiased embedding nearest-neighbor over visual impression alone.

reflection.text:
Unblinded specimen: emetine (CID 10219) - truth MoA Protein synthesis. Verdict correct on protocol, and my scientist call (p=0.62 Protein synthesis) was also correct. I am the Scientist reviewing after the protocol tally: 4/4 wells NSC Protein synthesis, summed similarity 3.126.

What got it right:
- Acquisition strategy and NSC comparison were decisive. I sampled a 100-fold window in one block: w_27f69f1427 30 uM, w_3856821e91 3 uM, w_086098dd16 1 uM, w_42421d2d9c 0.3 uM (e2, e3, e6, e7) after e1 showed 8 doses 0.01-30 uM available. All four wells independently returned nearest_moa Protein synthesis with similarities 0.699, 0.803, 0.813, 0.809. The 2-well interim (e5) and 4-well final (e11) were identical: NSC 2/2 then 4/4 Protein synthesis, k-neighbours 5/10 Protein synthesis, 3/10 Microtubule stabilizers, 1/10 Eg5. The protocol's 1-NN per well majority vote (Ljosa et al. 2013) correctly integrated this.
- Quantitative morphometrics were consistent and extreme across doses, not a high-dose artefact: nuc_solidity z=-38.2 to -55.0, nuc_form_factor z=-31.2 to -44.1, act_glcm_contrast z=+21.6 to +22.2, tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.3 at 30 uM, with persistence down to 0.3 uM where cell_count was still 414 vs 162 at 30 uM. That stability across e2/e3/e6/e7 argued for a single on-target MoA rather than progressive toxicity.
- Dose-response checks (e8, e9, e10, e13-e15) correctly prevented an Aurora miscall despite visual suggestion. e10 frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.20 (p=0.8) over those 4 wells showed no increase in multinucleation, contradicting Aurora kinase inhibitors / failed cytokinesis polyploidy. I noted this in hypothesis history step 12 as contradicting e11/e8 for Aurora, and kept Aurora at 0.23 only because of e4.
- Cell count trend 414 (0.3 uM) -> 364 (1 uM) -> 224 (3 uM) -> 162 (30 uM) was directionally consistent with protein synthesis cytostatic/cytotoxic effect, even though rho=-0.40 p=0.6 in e9 was underpowered with n=4 wells. I did not over-interpret the non-significant p-values (all e8-e15 p=0.2-0.8), which was correct given the design.

What misled / what I missed:
- e4 describe_phenotype was the main confounder: 'density lower vs DMSO; 7 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors'. The microscopist's free-text Aurora suggestion plus the large nuclear shape deviations (nuc_solidity/form_factor) can mimic enlarged irregular nuclei seen in Aurora, and the k-neighbour 3/10 Microtubule stabilizers in e5/e11 also introduced noise. I correctly down-weighted e4 because describe_phenotype is the softer free tool and NSC is the stricter feature-based test, but it still capped my confidence at 0.62 vs the protocol's 4-0 sweep.
- ChEMBL/PubChem lookup e17/e18 returned 'mechanisms: none curated (name and BBBC021 structure agree)' for emetine, so there was no curated MoA to anchor against during the blinded phase. I relied on morphology alone, which was appropriate. Post-unblinding literature search e19/e20 ('emetine protein synthesis inhibitor ribosome' 135 hits; 'emetine mechanism ... translation elongation' 35 hits) returns are consistent with emetine as a eukaryotic translation elongation/translocation inhibitor PMID 42539200, PMID 4949424, PMID 8618948, PMID 39293933, but during the blinded run I had no literature PMIDs to cite and made no claim - correct behavior.
- Acquisition choice limitation: I did not sample the lowest doses 0.01-0.1 uM. This did not change the call because the phenotype was already saturated at 0.3 uM (z=-33.1 for nuc_solidity), but it meant I could not define an EC50 or demonstrate emergence from baseline. The negative nuc_solidity rho=-0.80 e8 was actually driven by the most extreme value at 3 uM (-55.0) not a monotonic dose effect, which I recognized as non-significant.

Why: The measurement that mattered was the NSC similarity >0.80 at 0.3-3 uM, replicated in 4 independent wells, outweighing a single visual impression. The comparison that mattered was NSC vote vs describe_phenotype - I followed the protocol-specified NSC as primary. The acquisition that mattered was bracketing high (30 uM) and mid-low (0.3 uM) to test robustness, which succeeded.

Lesson: In this assay, nuclear solidity/form_factor collapse + actin/tubulin texture contrast increase can be shared between Protein synthesis and Aurora-like enlarged nuclei, so visual assessment alone (e4) is insufficient. Future lab follow-up as I proposed in e16 - orthogonal puromycin incorporation/SUnSET vs phospho-Histone H3 S10 plus DNA content flow cytometry with reference inhibitors - remains appropriate to discriminate translation shutdown from mitotic failure, even though the classifier was right here.
